Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an AI assistant that works through 32 registered tools. On 2026-11-20 and 21 Kenneth and I compared every upstream OrcaSlicer feature with those tools and read the kept production chats (386 chats, 89 people). Seven people asked the AI for something it could not do because no tool adds geometry: "add a cube", "add holes for the screws" (a wall bracket), "a cylinder with several holes", "a tube with a 2 mm wall", raised text reading "MICKEY", "add a little lip and put the SNAPON logo there", and text embossed onto a figure. Each was told to use another program. The full comparison is in the untracked file `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/ai-feature-coverage.md`.

Decisions Kenneth made, in his words. On the basis for grouping features into tools: "we need to use what it means to the users as the basis, not what it means inside the app, because no users cares about that." So adding a shape, a hole or text is one request, "changing the shape", and it is a separate tool from `region_annotate`, which says how an area of an object should print ("no support here", "seam off this face"). On this proposal, which read "The new tool: object_add_shape, described with 'hole', 'text' and the slicer terms 'part' and 'negative part'. The existing tool: rename it when the new tool is added, so names change once.", he wrote: "go with this proposal." On names he thinks the name matters to the model at least as much as the description, and "region" means nothing to him as a person; no one in the kept chats used that word. Two fresh agents asked to describe the tool in their own words said "mark a region of the surface" and "paint a region", which is why my candidate keeps "region" and drops "annotate". That candidate is mine and not confirmed.

How Kenneth wants to be worked with, learned the hard way in this conversation: check the written rule before proposing where something goes; hold a position until evidence changes it, and do not simply agree when he pushes back; start paid model runs at three; and never present an idea he has not approved as settled.

OrcaSlicer's own screens support the design: Add Part, Add Negative Part and Add Modifier each open the same list of Cube, Cylinder, Sphere, Cone, Disc, Torus, Text and SVG (`MenuFactory::append_menu_items_add_volume` in `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_Factories.cpp`), and a Change Type menu turns one into another. The branch `claude/unblock-hardware-settings` was being landed on `jusprin-dev` as this task was handed over; it changes the settings tools and the tool guide, not the region tool.

Task:
Build one new AI tool, `object_add_shape`, and rename the existing tool `region_annotate` in the same change, so tool names change once.

**What `object_add_shape` does.** It adds a shape to an existing object, in one undo step. Two inputs decide it: what the shape is for (a solid part, or a negative part, which is a hole) and what the shape is (a box, a cylinder, or text). A screw hole is "negative part, cylinder". Raised lettering is "part, text". Engraved lettering is "negative part, text". Sizes and positions are in millimetres in the world frame as the object stands now, the way `region_annotate` already takes boxes and cylinders. Follow the registry's existing conventions: `sessionId`, a result that lists the new part ids, `projectUndo`, and `regionsUnbound` when the change breaks a region's link to the geometry, as `object_divide` reports it.

**Name and describe it in the words of a request.** Use "add", "hole", "text", and the slicer terms "part" and "negative part". Use no internal word such as "volume". The description must also separate it from the existing kind `precision_hole`, which keeps support out of a hole that already exists and does not make one.

**The rename.** Rename `region_annotate` everywhere: registry, both adapters, tests, fixtures, the Agent page's instructions and skills, the guide pages and the tool guide's catalog. My candidate name is `object_mark_region`. Kenneth agreed to rename it but has not confirmed that exact name, so ask him to confirm it before you finalise. Do not change what the tool does.

**Text is the uncertain half. Check it first.** OrcaSlicer builds text as a background job, `start_create_volume` in `src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/EmbossJob.hpp`, normally driven from the text tool's own window (`Gizmos/GLGizmoEmboss.cpp`). Nobody has checked how much of that works without the window. Find out before designing. If text needs more than a small, product-neutral, additive seam in OrcaSlicer-owned files, build boxes and cylinders as parts and holes, and bring Kenneth what you found about text as a decision. Do not force it.

**Where to work.**
- Definitions: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`. Execution: `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`. The typed workspace interface: `Workspace/Workspace.hpp`.
- `Workspace/OrcaRegions.cpp` and `Workspace/Regions.hpp` already create modifier, support-blocker and support-enforcer volumes from a box or a cylinder (`volume_type`). Reuse that path for parts and negative parts; do not write a second one.
- The fake workspace and fixtures under `tests/jusprin_support/`; tests in `tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp`, `tests/workspace/test_workspace_contract.cpp` and the real-app harness `tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp`.
- `grep -rn region_annotate` over `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`, `tests`, `docs/guide` and `agent-docs` finds every place the old name appears.

**Rules to read before writing code.** `AGENTS.md`; `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`, above all "Required implementation sequence for one new tool", "Test matrix", "Naming and compatibility" and "Definition of done"; `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before any edit outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Start a new branch from `jusprin-dev` after pulling it, because the guide's renaming rule was changed on 2026-11-21 and must be in your base.

**Testing.** Unit tests and the real-app harness, including a check in the real app that a negative-part cylinder is really there after the call and is removed by project Undo. The harness has two failures that predate this work, `second_model_dropped` and `model_added_to_a_project_is_an_edit`; only a new name is yours. Write prompt cases from the real requests in the background below. Any run against a paid model needs Kenneth's yes first and starts at three conversations, never a runner's default count. Build with `-j4` on this shared Mac as `AGENTS.md` describes.

**Done looks like:** the tool is offered in the app and over MCP with the same definition; the real adapter adds parts and holes through OrcaSlicer's own owner of that state; the fake adapter matches; the rename is complete with no old name left; tests pass; the tool guide's catalog is updated; and Kenneth has a short report of what was tested, what was not, and the text finding. Do not push or land without asking him. Quote his words in the commit message.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_7a8aabaf-598d-4bd0-83a2-6844cad48410

Check whether text can be built without the window
Create branch from updated jusprin-dev
Add object_add_shape to registry, coordinator, adapters
Rename region_annotate everywhere
Write unit tests, harness check, prompt cases
Build and run tests and real-app harness
Report to Kenneth with name confirmation question

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

description: "2026-11-08 Kenneth: jusprin-dev is the development branch (cut from the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge 975c703f08); ui-walkthrough and jusprin-newui are superseded; tsd-enterprise server code straight to master"

---

From 2026-11-08, JusPrin app work lands on `jusprin-dev`. Kenneth: "branch out a jusprin-dev from the upstream merge commit, and use this branch as the dev branch". It starts at `975c703f08` (the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 into ui-walkthrough) and contains `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those. AGENTS.md's "Branches" section records this. `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1. Server code in tsd-enterprise goes straight to `master` (2026-11-06 rule, unchanged).

History: 2026-11-06 `jusprin-newui-integration`; 2026-11-07 `ui-walkthrough`; 2026-11-08 `jusprin-dev`.

`main`, Kenneth 2026-11-08: "main will be the stable branch that doesn't allow force push ( except in some extreme circumstances when no other options are feasible). This is so that the users who clone our repo won't have to force pull." and "for now, it also double a release branch. But this rule is more flexible than the first one." GitHub branch protection on `main` blocks force pushes and deletion, admins included (enforce_admins). `main` moves forward from `jusprin-dev` only when a version is released; ask before fast-forwarding it. On 2026-11-08 Kenneth chose to leave `main` at 4da9d7beb4 until 2.0.0 ships, although that means the scheduled nightly keeps running `main`'s older file and doesn't build `jusprin-dev` until then. Start the nightly by hand on `jusprin-dev` with only `-f sign_macos=true`. GitHub runs scheduled workflows from `main`'s copy of the file, and validates dispatch inputs against it.

**Why:** the dev branch is the build Kenneth reviews; work on a side branch never reaches what he tests.

**How to apply:** Kenneth, 2026-11-08: "I want the main checkout to be always on jusprin-dev". Since then /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin holds `jusprin-dev`; byoai-newui was moved to its own branch `byoai-newui`. Git allows one checkout per branch, so never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. Commit from a worktree of your own on its own branch or detached at the tip. Then bring the main checkout along so its files match the branch; moving the ref from elsewhere (update-ref, or a push without a pull) leaves the main checkout's `git status` showing the new commits as reversed. When pushing is asked: push to origin jusprin-dev, then `git -C /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin pull --ff-only` (Kenneth: "you just need to bring the local main checkout by pulling from the remote"). Push nothing unless asked. Supersedes the landing question in [[merge-no-ff-not-squash]].

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

name: group-tools-by-user-meaning
description: "Kenneth 2026-11-21: group features into AI tools by what they mean to the person, not by how the app makes them; and check the placement rules before proposing where a fact goes"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Kenneth, 2026-11-21, on how to group OrcaSlicer features into AI tools: "I'm pretty sure we need to use what it means to the users as the basis, not what it means inside the app, because no users cares about that." The tool guide already says it (`mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`: "A tool does one thing that a slicer user has a name for").

**Why:** in one day I moved holes, shapes and text between "own tool", "region tool" and back three times, each time on an argument about mechanism (they are all volumes with a type) or because he pushed. He said "Don't just go along with whatever I said." Two cold-reader agents grouped by mechanism when asked for tools and by meaning when asked how a user thinks; the user grouping put holes and text with cutting ("changing the shape") and blocker shapes with support painting ("supports").

**How to apply:**
- For a grouping question, ask what the person would call the thing they want, and group by that. How OrcaSlicer builds it is not the basis.
- State my own position with its evidence and where I disagree; do not flip because he questioned it. Change it only on new evidence, and say what the evidence was.
- Before proposing where a sentence for the model goes, apply [[rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs]] and the every-turn test in [[prompt-principles-vs-state-channels]]. On 2026-11-21 I proposed a system-prompt line for one setting's name (bed size is `printable_area`) without checking; it fails the every-turn test, and he caught it.
- Paid runs start small: [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]].

**Names (same day):** Kenneth thinks a tool's name matters to the model even more than its description, and that the guide's "Do not rename a released tool without a strong reason" is probably a wrong rule. Traced: that sentence came in with commit 644f8bfaff (2026-09-04, the first MCP bridge) as general API practice; I found no words of his behind it, and tools have been renamed or retired since (duplicate_object, import_model, intent_update) with no incident. Do not cite it against a rename. What a rename really costs: an outside AI tool's saved permission for the old name lapses; saved in-app chats keep working. I had claimed "the model reads the description more than the name" with no evidence; a search found Anthropic's docs calling the description the most important factor, one paper (BiasBusters, ICLR 2026) saying the match between the request's words and the tool's name and description drives selection, and no study isolating name from description. So: word names and descriptions in the words of the request, or the slicer term a model already knows, never an internal code word.

name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

**Start small (Kenneth, 2026-11-21, angry):** "do you really have to run it 20 times? Start small... If you had only run it 3 times and none of the happened, you already knew that it's not working." I had run `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --case change-bed-size` with no `--runs`, which defaults to 20 for a single case (968k input tokens); it failed 19 of 20, and 3 runs would have shown the same.
**How to apply:** for any paid model run, pass `--runs 3` (or the smallest count the runner allows) first, even after he says "run it". Go to more runs only when the small run is mixed and the difference matters, and say the count before starting. Never rely on a runner's default count.

result.output:
# Guide for adding JusPrin tools

**Status:** This guide explains how to add a tool to JusPrin. The three things it builds on are already implemented: the shared tool registry, the MCP server embedded in the app, and the stdio bridge (a small helper program that connects external AI clients to that server). Over MCP, the tools currently cover inspecting the workspace, reporting on a slice for review, and the settings workflow. The settings workflow works on the process preset, on one object, and on filament and printer presets. Later in this guide there is a [candidate catalog](#candidate-catalog): a list of tools we might build, worked out from the product's screens. It follows the implemented catalog record. Nothing in the candidate catalog exists unless the catalog record says it does.

JusPrin has one tool system. A new capability is defined once, in the shared registry. `ToolExecutionCoordinator` runs it. Its implementation reads and changes the open project through the typed workspace interface. Two adapters, one for OpenAI and one for MCP, only translate that single definition into the format each side expects. The aim of this guide is a tool catalog that stays small, does only what it claims to do, can change safely over time, and is shaped by real printing tasks. It should not be shaped by a list of every feature OrcaSlicer has.

Treat this guide as the starting point. Change it when what you learn from implementing, from real MCP clients, or from evals shows that a rule, a contract, a limit, or a sequence here should change. Do not keep a planning assumption just because it is written here. Base every revision on evidence, and describe significant changes in the PR. Two things do not change: OrcaSlicer stays the owner of the state it owns, and the verification requirements stay.

Before you touch any OrcaSlicer class that holds live state, read [the production documentation](README.md), [production architecture](architecture.md), and [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md). The current tool definitions are in [`ToolRegistry.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp). The code that runs them is in [`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp). The code that presents them over MCP is in [`McpProtocol.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp).

External clients on the same machine connect through the bundled `jusprin-mcp` stdio helper, which is set up from **Connect AI tools...**. The helper and the server inside the app are compiled from the same registry. So every new tool you offer must have the same catalog entry and the same schema whether the app is running (live) or not (offline), for the same build and the same negotiated protocol version. Do not add a catalog that exists in only one adapter. Connecting to the server directly over HTTP is a route for developers. It is not what the default setup instructions tell people to do.

## Words this guide uses

- **Registry.** The one list of tool definitions, compiled into the app (`ToolRegistry.cpp`).
- **Catalog.** The list of tools as a caller sees it.
- **Coordinator.** `ToolExecutionCoordinator`, the class that queues tool calls and runs them on the GUI thread.
- **Workspace.** The typed C++ interface (`IWorkspace`) through which JusPrin reads and changes the open project. It has two implementations, called workspace adapters. The real one works on live OrcaSlicer. The fake one is for tests.
- **Tool adapter.** Code that translates registry definitions and results for one kind of caller. There are two: the in-app adapter, which uses OpenAI's format and serves the Agent panel, and the MCP adapter, which serves external clients. "Both adapters" in this guide means these two.
- **Projection.** The form in which one tool adapter presents a definition or a result.
- **Exposure.** The registry setting that says which callers are offered a tool.
- **Owner.** The OrcaSlicer class that holds the real copy of some state, or that already implements an operation.
- **Seam.** A small addition to a file OrcaSlicer owns, which lets fork code call or observe OrcaSlicer's behavior.
- **Session and revision.** `sessionId` identifies the project that is currently open. `revision` is a counter the workspace raises when its state changes. A call that was prepared against an older session or revision is called stale.
- **Action class.** Whether a tool is read-only, a mutation (it changes something), or destructive.
- **Dirty.** A preset is dirty when it has unsaved edits.
- **Eval.** An automated test that gives a model a task and checks the transcript that results.
- **M0 to M5.** The milestones in which the tool catalog was delivered.

## Current connection and execution boundary

- The server starts automatically with the JusPrin Agent panel. There is no `JUSPRIN_MCP` switch to enable it and no bearer token. The server listens only on the numeric loopback address. It prefers port 47301, and falls back to a port chosen by the operating system only when 47301 is taken.
- The shell tells the server where its discovery file is: `<data_dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`. The running server writes its details there in one atomic step: the actual address, the PID, a unique `instanceId` for this run, the build version, and the protocol versions. Before a server removes the record, it checks, while holding the discovery lock, that the record is its own. An older server therefore cannot remove a newer server's record, even inside the same process. On POSIX systems the file has mode `0600`.
- The helper checks that the discovery file is valid, and then tests that the address in it answers. When the app starts or restarts later, the helper follows the new record. The helper never launches JusPrin. The discovery file holds one record, and the last server to write it wins. So the helper works with one selected instance; there is no way to choose among several. `--discovery`, `JUSPRIN_MCP_DISCOVERY`, and `JUSPRIN_MCP_URL` override the file path or the address. They do not switch anything on. The connection entries that Connect writes use `--discovery` with the app's actual data directory.
- When the app is not running, the helper answers discovery and tool-list requests from the registry compiled into the helper. Tool calls made while the app is not running return `workspace_unavailable`. When the app can be reached, the helper uses the app's live catalog and results, even when the app and the helper are different versions. Do not replace a live app's tool list with the helper's compiled one. A version difference between the two is logged.
- The HTTP adapter accepts MCP protocol version `2026-07-28`. The helper can also negotiate the older versions `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18`, and `2025-11-25`. The helper does all conversion between versions. Code that executes a tool must not behave differently for different protocol versions.
- **Connect** shows the person the command or the file edit and asks for confirmation first. Then it either runs the Claude Code or Codex CLI, or merges the JusPrin entry into the JSON configuration of Claude Desktop/local Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. A JSON edit keeps unrelated settings and makes a backup. It is refused when the preview is out of date or when the destination is a symlink. It does not protect against another editor writing the same file at the exact moment of replacement.
- On macOS the helper is bundled next to the app executable. Windows has a matching install rule. On Linux, the entry for an AppImage uses the installed image's path plus `--mcp-bridge`, and the app handles that flag before the GUI starts. Do not save a temporary AppImage mount path as the command.

Workspace commands run on the GUI thread, through the shared coordinator. A timer owned by the shell keeps execution moving, so execution does not depend on the WebView's handshake. No external client ever gets direct access to OrcaSlicer objects.

A call from an external client is tagged `ToolSource::Mcp`. The MCP adapter sets that tag, so it can be trusted, and it is kept for the activity history and for diagnostics. External calls run through the same coordinator and the same workspace commands as calls from the in-app Agent. The change log records the edits they make, as it records every edit, and marks them `external`. In the conversation thread those edits appear as rows that say "External tool", where a change made in the app says "Agent".

## Start with an eval failure

The fact that OrcaSlicer has a menu item or a config key is not a reason to add a tool. Start from a transcript or an automated eval in which the Agent cannot finish a real user task, finishes it only some of the time, or needs an unreasonable number of steps or tokens.

Write down:

- what the user wanted to achieve;
- the exact point where the current tools stop being enough;
- which OrcaSlicer state or operation is missing;
- what a successful transcript should look like;
- the unsafe or ambiguous cases that must fail; and
- the evidence that will show the new tool fixed the problem.

If the failure can be fixed by a clearer description, a better result, or a more useful validation error, improve the existing definition instead of adding a tool.

The candidate catalog later in this guide lists tools we might build. Being listed there does not accept a tool, and it does not excuse a tool from this section. A row in that catalog does two jobs. It records which product screen and which group of evals the tool would serve, which makes the eval easier to write. It also settles what the tool acts on, its action class, and its OrcaSlicer owner, so that two people do not build the same capability twice under different names.

## Tool budget and tool shape

The limit on the number of tools comes from how much the model has to load on each turn. It does not come from how much the app can do. The rules in this section rest on this evidence:

- OpenAI's function-calling guidance keeps fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn and defers the rest.
- Anthropic's [tool-writing guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents) asks for a few tools aimed at high-impact workflows. It names "tools that merely wrap existing software functionality or API endpoints" as the common error.
- A [domain-oriented MCP study](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22063v1) measured three interfaces. A generic interface of thin tools scored below raw SQL. Tools shaped around the domain scored far above both.
- The "god tool", one tool that dispatches many unrelated actions through a single `action` parameter, is a documented anti-pattern.

The current five-tool MCP catalog measures about 1.9 KB per definition, and two thirds of that is output schema.

**How tools are loaded for now.** Both adapters load every registered tool on every turn. The in-app adapter sends the full function list with each request, and MCP `tools/list` returns the whole catalog. This is the simplest behaviour that is correct. It also keeps the tools array byte-identical through a chat, and OpenAI's prompt cache depends on exactly that. The budget is 20 definitions per turn. Going over 20 does not block anything. It is the point at which we start watching the measurements. The live regression test records definition bytes, input tokens, and cached tokens for each request. The journey catalog below goes over 20 definitions from its first milestone. We accept that until those measurements show the model selecting wrong tools or running short of context.

**The baseline, measured on Windows against the live app.**

| After milestone | In-app definitions | In-app bytes | MCP definitions | MCP bytes | MCP bytes through the offline helper recipe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| M0 | 7 | 3,145 | 5 | 3,147 | |
| M1 | 11 | 6,482 | 9 | 6,915 | |
| M2 | 18 | 12,721 | 16 | 13,911 | 13,894 |
| M3 | 20 | 19,331 | 21 | 22,661 | 22,639 |
| M4 | 20 | 21,594 | 21 | 24,923 | 24,901 |
| M5 | 25 | 29,148 | 26 | 33,013 | |

The M5 figure for MCP was read over two `tools/list` pages.

The `--live-agent` regression test, run at M0 and at M1, shows what those definitions cost in tokens. The first request of a conversation gets nothing from the cache and pays for the whole catalog: 803 tokens at M0 and 1,733 at M1. So four more definitions cost about 930 tokens, paid once. Every later request in the same conversation came back 77 to 92 per cent cached (at M1, 5,864 input tokens, of which 5,376 were cached). That is because the tools array is byte-identical through a chat, and the cache depends on that. At M2, the same test made eleven requests that took 2,875 to 6,763 input tokens, with 42 to 91 per cent cached. None of the eleven started with an empty cache, because an earlier run on the same day had already cached the shared beginning of the prompt. So that run did not measure the uncached cost at M2.

The conclusion is that a definition adds cost to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn. That is why going over the budget only makes us look at the measurements and does not block a tool. Two things would change this conclusion: a catalog so large that the first request of every conversation is expensive by itself, or transcripts that show the model choosing the wrong tool. Watch for both. Neither has appeared yet.

**The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set of tools.** The printer panel on Home runs its own conversation, `PrinterConversation`. That conversation is offered the five printer tools and the four settings tools. The list is the same in every mode (Add, Change, or Connect), so it stays byte-identical through a conversation and between conversations of the same mode.

One tool is added during a conversation, on purpose. `issue_report_open` comes with either connection skill, `connect-bambu` or `connect-print-host` (`PrinterConversation::connection_skill`, carried as `AgentSkillUse::tools`). It is offered from the request where the skill is first sent, including the continuation after the tool result that brought the skill, and on every request after that. The skill, and so the tool, comes into force once the chat has a saved printer: with `printer_add`'s result, or on the first request of a chat about one. A chat with no saved printer never has it. Adding it costs that chat one prompt-cache miss, and that cost was accepted. The list stays the same from then on. This is not deferral: no tool search, no `defer_loading`, and no toolsets. The app decides when the tool is offered, and the model never asks for it.

What a call may do depends on the conversation. `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses every call that is not allowed, before any card is shown, with an error that says where to go instead. The rules are:

- Finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`) is allowed only in an Add conversation. A Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has. An add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it.
- `printer_change` is allowed only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one. When the project uses that printer, its unsaved edits are dropped and listed in `discarded`; the panel's coordinator saves a version first, as the project's agent pane does for any change to the project. If that save fails, the call does not run and returns the coordinator's generic `local_save_failed`; there is no separate message for it.
- The connection tools are allowed only once there is a saved printer.
- The settings tools are allowed only with `scope: "printer"`, on the printer the conversation is about.

A Change conversation may be about a stock profile (one that ships with OrcaSlicer) that the project has selected. That happens when the person chooses Printer settings… in the header on a project that uses a stock profile. In that case, changes to the nozzle and to the connection are refused with `stock_profile`. Changes to settings are saved as a copy of the profile, and the conversation follows that copy from then on (`PrinterConversation::tool_settled`). A Change conversation is never turned into an Add conversation. The code that opens a Change conversation checks that the printer is there, and shows OrcaSlicer's error dialog when it is not.

The header's filament chat uses the same panel (`PrinterPanel::open_filament`). It is offered the four settings tools and nothing else, and it gets no project state. It has its own instructions. The page writes them in `AgentUI/src/filamentInstructions.ts` and sends them with `filament_instructions`. The page writes them from the facts the app sends as the session part of the panel's state (`PrinterPanel::filament_session_json`): the preset's name, its slot and material, and, for a stock filament, the copy that a change is saved as. The preflight check for this chat allows the settings tools only with `scope: "filament"` on that preset. It refuses an apply that has no `persistAs`, with `not_saved`, because the chat is gone when it closes. When a copy is saved in the preset's place, the chat is about that copy from then on, and the page writes the instructions again for the copy. Until 2026-09-29 the filament chat ran on the project assistant's instructions and tools. With those, the model read "make the nozzle 5 degrees hotter" as a request to print. In another run it set 205 °C when the value was 220 °C, without reading the value first.

We do not give each mode a different tool list, for two reasons. The conversation has to refuse disallowed calls anyway, whatever list the model is shown. And the way to restrict tools while keeping the list stable (`tool_choice` with `allowed_tools`) exists only on some providers. We would reconsider if transcripts showed the model reaching for a refused tool and then failing to recover. `tests/printer_prompt` measures this with the `change-add-another` case.

Two past changes explain the current design:

- Until 2026-09-23 the panel offered one tool per mode (7f66e75b07). The reason was to keep a printer lookup from clearing the pinned card of the printer a Change session was about. That card is gone (4d4f9e466b). Offering one tool per step also left an Add conversation with no tool to connect the printer it had just added (8334b3395b).
- On 2026-09-28 three tools were removed (b60fc2d8e6): `printer_manual_setup`, `printer_manual_connection` and `printer_setup_finish`. These were the tools that opened a window or closed the panel. The full printer list (the printer form since 2026-10-20, or OrcaSlicer's own list when the panel's page cannot load) and a printer's settings are still reachable from the panel's own buttons, and the person closes the panel.

The app decides which tools are offered. The page writes the text: `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` holds the instructions, and `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts` holds the notes the model reads after a tap. If a turn arrives before the page has written its instructions, the app refuses the turn. The app has no prompt of its own to send instead. The instructions for an Add conversation carry the whole printer list, about 28 KB. That text is always the same and sits at the start of the instructions, so it is cached. No printer conversation carries the project: no workspace state goes into the turn, and none goes into a tool result.

**Deferral, when the measurements say so.** Deferral means the model first sees only a short index and loads a tool's full definition when it needs it. Use the deferral feature that the model platform provides. Never write our own mechanism for switching tools in and out. For the in-app Agent, the platform feature is OpenAI's `tool_search` with `defer_loading: true` on the Responses API. It is documented for `gpt-5.4` and later. Whether it works on the pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` has not been verified. On the MCP side, clients defer by themselves, as Claude Code does. Tools would be deferred one toolset at a time (toolsets are the named groups in the candidate catalog), and OpenAI recommends fewer than ten functions per namespace. Do not build a tool that enables a toolset by rewriting the tools array. Every switch would break the prompt cache.

**Shape each tool as a domain operation.** A tool does one thing that a slicer user has a name for: place an object, lay out the plates, mark a region, set up the printer. Do not wrap each OrcaSlicer function in its own tool. Do not build a tool that interprets a list of unrelated commands. One operation may have several optional facets, as long as each facet has its own type and the tool rejects facets that conflict.

**Batch only where items share a shape.** Good examples are a list of setting changes, a list of annotations, and a list of layout rows with one row per object. A list that mixes transforms, imports, and deletes is the god tool described above. It is refused.

**Fold reads into sections and detail levels before adding a read tool.** A new read tool is justified in only two cases. Either its inputs are of a different kind (a search over a large catalog, an analysis of one object, a report on a sliced plate), or its result is an image.

**Let call logs decide consolidation.** If transcripts show that two tools are always called together, consider merging them. If two facets of one tool are never used together, consider splitting them. Make these decisions from eval evidence, not from a design discussion.

**Output schemas are not advertised over MCP.** No client was shown to use them, and they were two thirds of the catalog. `tools/list` no longer carries `outputSchema`. `validate_output` still checks every successful MCP result, so a result that breaks its contract still fails with a visible error. We measured the effect on one build, with the recipe near the end of this guide. With five tools, the catalog went from 9,723 bytes to 3,141, which is from about 2,430 tokens to 785. Only the MCP side saves anything. The in-app adapter has always sent `input_schema` as `parameters` and nothing else, so an in-app turn never carried output schemas. Restore the field only for a client that is shown to read it.

## Choose the narrowest honest scope

Do not put an enum value in a schema, such as one of `printer | filament | process | object`, unless every advertised value works in both the fake and the real workspace adapter and inherits values the way the documentation says.

For each proposed capability, answer:

1. Which OrcaSlicer owner holds the real state or performs the operation?
2. Is the command valid for the whole project, one plate, one object, one instance, or one preset layer?
3. What stable ID identifies the target, and when does that ID expire?
4. Which revision must still be current when the command executes?
5. Which existing OrcaSlicer undo snapshot covers the change, and how is the change undone, reset, or reverted? Or does ordinary project Undo not apply?
6. Which workspace change reasons tell readers that they must read again?
7. What happens if the user edits something in the GUI while the call is queued or running?

If any of these answers is unclear, the tool's contract is not ready.

## Reuse the one authority path

Every change to the project must take this route:

```text
adapter call
→ shared registry validation
→ ToolExecutionCoordinator queue
→ immediate execution
→ IWorkspace command
→ current Orca owner
→ Orca history and state change
→ coalesced workspace event
→ fresh snapshot/result
```

A tool adapter must not call `Plater`, `Model`, `PresetBundle`, wxWidgets, or slicing objects directly. Do not copy an OrcaSlicer operation into JusPrin. If the operation you need exists only inside OrcaSlicer's UI code, add the smallest possible seam to the class that currently owns the operation. Name the seam for what it does, and put nothing JusPrin-specific in it.

Any change to a file OrcaSlicer owns must follow [fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Keep the diff small, and add lines instead of rewriting existing ones. Record why the seam belongs where you put it, identify the upstream lines you touched, and include the rebase evidence.

## JusPrin-owned project state

Some product state is not held anywhere in OrcaSlicer: the print's purpose, the pinned agent plan, semantic region annotations, physical facts the user confirmed about a printer, and the monitoring rules the user sets for automatic pausing. For this state, the "current Orca owner" step in the route above is a JusPrin store instead. Every other step stays the same. The rules are:

- **Storage.** State that belongs to a project (purpose, plan, regions, conversation, and attachments) lives in the local project store, under a project ID that does not change. The current `ProjectStateDocument` is saved separately from model checkpoints. An imported project may contain the older `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json`. It is read only to migrate it. In that document:
  - each chat owns its purpose, the setup title `setupIntent` (with the purpose setup beside it), and its plan, `plan`. The project's current purpose and plan are the active chat's, read through `activeConversationId` and stored nowhere else; a new chat starts with a copy of the active chat's purpose and no plan. A plan write replaces the whole plan. A chat's `printIntent`, the requirement fields `setup_record` kept until 2026-10-25, is no longer read or copied; a document that holds one loads as before;
  - the region annotations, `regions`, describe the model in the workspace. A write replaces the whole list, and each record is stamped with a seq when it changes. Every saved model version records the list it was saved with, and restoring or resuming that version puts its list back.

  State that belongs to a printer (confirmed facts, monitoring policy) stays in app data, stored per printer identity, the way `PrinterFactsStore` keeps it. Confirmed facts carry an expiry, because the physical world changes without telling the app. See [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md).
- **Revision.** Every write has to signal that it happened, so that readers read again. Two questions are still **open**: which signal to use, and whether the signal invalidates actions that are already queued. They belong to the milestone that adds the first writer. The obvious answer would be to publish a `WorkspaceChangeReasons` bit and add that bit to `kInvalidatingReasons`. That cannot be built as described. `settings_apply_patch` requires its caller's `expectedRevision` to equal the current revision exactly. So if the revision goes up at any point between a client's preview and its apply, the apply fails as `stale_workspace`. An agent that recorded its plan between previewing and applying would make its own call fail. There is an existing example of the alternative: the edit feed (`WorkspaceEditHub`) reports a change without raising the revision. Decide separately for each kind of state. A region annotation generates OrcaSlicer artifacts, so it is a real change to the project. A purpose, or a statement of the plan, is not. In the code as built, writing a region record signals nothing by itself. The artifacts it generates are ordinary OrcaSlicer edits, and they raise the revision in the usual way. So an action that was queued before an annotation goes stale, exactly as it would after any other edit to the model.
- **Undo.** None of this state is in OrcaSlicer's undo stack. Results say `projectUndo: false`. Region annotations are the awkward case. They generate OrcaSlicer artifacts (modifier volumes, enforcers, blockers, paint), and those artifacts *are* in the undo stack. So project Undo can leave an annotation without its artifacts, or leave an artifact without its annotation. The `regions` section of `object_analyze` reports both situations, and `region_annotate` generates the artifacts again. The result of a place, divide, or repair lists the regions whose link to the geometry that operation broke.
- **Provenance (where a value came from).** Any field that records a fact about the world or about what the user wants also records its source: `file` (read from the project or a profile), `observed` (reported by a sensor or the printer, with a timestamp), `agent_inferred`, or `user_confirmed`. A tool marks a value `user_confirmed` only when the call is based on something the user explicitly said. Values the agent inferred stay `agent_inferred`. A value only the model writes, with nothing in the app that confirms it, cannot be `user_confirmed`: `setup_record`'s requirement fields were stored that way and fed back to the model each turn as the person's facts, and were removed on 2026-10-25. When a tool reads printer state, it reports the `configured` value and the `observed` value of the same fact separately, and it computes the `mismatches` between them itself. That comparison is not left to the model.

## Define the contract before the implementation

For every new tool, the registry entry, together with its contract and tests, must specify:

- a name that will not change, in lowercase with underscores;
- a short title, shown in the activity UI;
- a short description that says when to use the tool;
- a strict JSON Schema for the input, with `additionalProperties: false` where practical;
- a JSON Schema for the output;
- its `ActionClass`, which is trusted because it is set in the registry;
- whether it is offered to the in-app Agent, to MCP, or to both;
- what must be true for it to be available, such as an open FFF project (FFF is ordinary filament printing) or a selected object;
- whether the action is revision-sensitive, meaning it must fail when the workspace has changed since it was requested;
- whether it applies completely or not at all, and how it is really undone, reset, or reverted. Say so explicitly

## Decide whether this should be a tool

Add or extend a tool when the Agent needs one of three things: up-to-date state read straight from OrcaSlicer, a calculation that OrcaSlicer does and that always gives the same answer for the same input, or a change to the live project.

Do not add a tool for:

- a single setting key. Setting keys are records that the generic settings tools search and edit;
- general printing advice that the model can work out from a skill;
- a fixed bundle of changes such as "make it stronger", where the right answer depends on the part and on what the user cares about;
- driving the UI, such as pressing a button or operating a widget or a hidden panel;
- data that an existing tool already returns in a size-limited result;
- a capability someone might want in the future, with no eval or user task behind it; or
- an operation that the real workspace adapter cannot truly perform through the OrcaSlicer class that owns it.

A fixed, mechanical step of a workflow can be a tool. Examples are generating OrcaSlicer's calibration geometry and starting OrcaSlicer's slice action. Advice should stay a skill until there is a separately specified operation behind it that always behaves the same way.

## Prefer extending nouns over multiplying verbs

The settings workflow has four operations that do not change. They work on searchable data, whichever preset layer the values belong to:

```text
settings_search → settings_get → settings_preview_patch → settings_apply_patch
```

Do not create one tool per setting:

```text
set_layer_height
set_wall_loops
set_infill_density
set_support_angle
```

The same rule applies to presets, project objects, plates, warnings, and slice reports. Extend the typed records that describe them, and the size-limited tools that query them, before you create dozens of special-purpose actions.

A new operation deserves its own tool when it really differs from the existing ones in at least one of these ways: which action class it belongs to (read-only, mutation or destructive), whether it applies completely or not at all, how it starts, runs, and ends, or what its result means. `slice_start` is an example. It is not one more way to change settings. It starts OrcaSlicer work that runs in the background, and it completes in a different way from a settings change. That difference justifies a separate tool.

Split an operation into a preview tool and an apply tool only where OrcaSlicer may rewrite, replace, or refuse what the caller asked for. In those cases the caller has to see what would really happen before submitting the change. There are three such cases:

- settings, because OrcaSlicer's normalizer (the code that adjusts dependent settings after an edit) can rewrite values;
- preset selection, because OrcaSlicer may substitute a compatible preset, and dirty edits may be lost;
- topology changes such as cutting, splitting, or merging, because the caller needs to see the resulting pieces.

Sending a print is not a fourth. The agent opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog, which shows the person the slot mapping and the printer's readiness, and the person presses Send there (see [Sending a print](product-definition.md#29-sending-a-print)).

Everywhere else, the coordinator computes and validates the resulting state as part of the call. If a preview would only repeat its input back, do not make it a tool.

Prefer read tools whose results have a fixed, typed shape. Avoid one general record search whose result changes shape. Each section of `workspace_inspect` keeps its own fixed shape. A generic `records_search` whose result shape depends on a `kind` argument would make the model guess what comes back.
